t: You're standing where the Middlesex Hospital once stood in Fitzrovia. It was a teaching hospital that moved to Mortimer Street in 1757 and closed in 2005. Its Broderip Ward, opened in 1987, was the first in the UK dedicated to people with HIV and AIDS. Many well-known people died here, among them the comedian Peter Sellers, the evolutionary biologist W. D. Hamilton and the occultist Dion Fortune. The financier Horatio Bottomley also died here. The novelist Lisa Jewell was born here.
